points.description: Asynchronous transmission is described as character-by-character transmission: each character is a self-contained unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit. Equivalent wording is accepted. It is simple and cheap but gives lower transmission rates. Full marks need the start/stop framing, and the low-rate or cheap trade-off is not required.

Synchronous transmission is described as characters grouped into a continuous stream of data in frames, with frame boundaries marked by SYN or flag bytes. Equivalent wording is accepted. It is more complex, gives higher transmission rates, and requires synchronization between sender and receiver. Full marks need the grouped-frames idea with SYN/flag delimiting; the complexity, rate and synchronization points are supporting detail.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both modes to be described correctly: asynchronous as self-contained characters with start/stop bits, and synchronous as frames delimited by SYN or flag with sender-receiver synchronization. Each point is all-or-nothing. A response that swaps the two descriptions or describes only one mode earns no mark for the missing or swapped point.
